nodes.name: Check Existing Statement
nodes.notes: MANUAL VERIFICATION REQUIRED AFTER IMPORT: confirm the getAll/filter parameter names against the installed Supabase node version. Requires statements.source_message_id column (see idempotency SQL). This node's result now feeds a 3-way resolution ('IF Statement Exists' -> 'Check Statement Processing Status'), so it must return the full row (or at minimum id, source_message_id, processing_status) -- not just id/source_message_id as in the original Phase D draft. If your Supabase node config restricts returned columns, add processing_status to that list explicitly. alwaysOutputData=true so the downstream IF always has exactly one item to branch on even on 0 matches -- on 0 matches it passes through the original (id-less) input item; on 1 match it returns the matched statements row.

nodes.name: Check Statement Processing Status
nodes.notes: Branches on the EXISTING parent statements row's processing_status. 'completed' -> genuine duplicate, stop cleanly. Anything else (processing, review, error, or any other non-completed value your schema supports) -> resume the same row rather than creating a second parent. If you later add a distinct terminal failure/review status that should NOT be auto-resumed, split this into a 3-way switch -- kept as a single IF here per the requested minimal, targeted change.

nodes.name: Restore Original Item + Binary
nodes.notes: Rejoins the untouched original 'Extract Email Metadata' item (input 0 -- carries $binary.attachment_0 plus bank_name/message_id/subject/sender_email/timestamp/detection) with the tail of the idempotency + canonical-category branch (input 1, from 'Normalize Canonical Categories'). Required because Check Existing Statement, Create Statement, Resume Existing Statement, Set Statement Context, Load Canonical Categories and Normalize Canonical Categories all replace or narrow the item's json and none of them return binary data -- without this merge, 'Extract Password for Bank' would lose both $json.bank_name (and message_id/subject/sender_email/timestamp) AND $binary.attachment_0. statement_id and canonical_categories are unaffected either way since everything downstream reads those via $('Set Statement Context')/$('Normalize Canonical Categories') named references, not through this chain -- this merge exists purely to carry the original item + binary forward to the parser step. Applies identically to both the new-statement and resumed-statement branches, since both converge through Set Statement Context and this same canonical-category lookup before reaching here.

nodes.name: Get Statement Transactions
nodes.notes: Phase 3 fix (Issue 1): authoritative read of ALL statement_transactions rows for this statement_id, replacing Aggregate Statement Totals' prior use of $input.all(). executeOnce=true is required -- this node sits in the per-transaction item stream (one item per row Create a row just inserted); without executeOnce it would re-run once per transaction and multiply the aggregation. statement_id only -- never statement_month or transaction_date.

nodes.name: Resolve Account: Get Accounts
nodes.notes: Phase 4 fix: fetches all accounts for the single owner once (constant per execution). Aggregate Statement Totals matches this statement's card_last4/account_last4 + bank_name against these rows to resolve statements.account_id. No institution match, no guess: 0 or >1 candidates leaves account_id null.

nodes.name: Create Account If Missing
nodes.notes: Only reached when account_match_status === 'no_match' (unambiguous, just never seen before). Never reached for 'ambiguous' -- that status is never auto-created, per explicit instruction.
